propositions.text: Credibility findings cannot be solely based on objective country conditions without considering applicants' narrative non-credible findings.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds credibility findings cannot rely only on country conditions without considering applicants' narrative issues.

propositions.text: Applicants seek judicial review under subsection 72(1) IRPA of RPD decision rejecting refugee claim under sections 96 and 97 IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the applicants seek judicial review of the RPD decision rejecting their refugee claim under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: Applicants are Muhammad Siddique Khurram (36), Fatima Muhammad Khurram (34), Hamza (6), Omar (5), all Pakistani citizens.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the applicants are Pakistani citizens Muhammad Siddique Khurram, Fatima Muhammad Khurram, and their two children.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant is Sunni Muslim; wife is Shia Muslim; married 2009; returned to UAE for work; traveled to Pakistan Oct 2012 for son's medical treatment.
Principal Applicant alleges abduction in Pakistan Nov 7, 2012 by Islamic organization due to interfaith marriage; released after leaving package in Shia mosque.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal applicant is Sunni, wife Shia, married 2009, traveled to Pakistan in 2012; applicant alleges abduction due to marriage.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant alleges police refused to take complaint Nov 8, 2012; fled to Dubai Nov 9; visa applications to Canada denied; traveled UK June 2014.
In Jan 2015, obtained US visas; Canadian visitor visas again rejected Feb 2015; began receiving threatening texts from abductors.
Wife and children victims of two intentional car accidents; did not report incidents or texts to UAE authorities fearing deportation; incidents related.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges police refused complaint, fled to Dubai, visa denials, threats, intentional accidents, and fear of reporting due to deportation risk.

propositions.text: Applicants left Dubai May 31, 2015, arrived Canada June 2, 2015; Principal Applicant alleges continued threatening texts in Canada; did not report to Canadian authorities.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges continued threats after arriving in Canada but did not report them to authorities.

propositions.text: RPD decision Sept 15, 2015: Applicants not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
RPD found Applicants not credible except basic facts about religion and citizenship.
RPD found Principal Applicant's abduction story not plausible; police refusal to register complaint unsupported by evidence.
RPD found Applicants' claim of inability to approach UAE authorities not credible; no evidence of deportation risk due to wife's Shia status.
RPD found implausible that Principal Applicant did not change phone number in UAE and Canada despite threats; did not believe threatening texts in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the applicants not credible, rejected abduction story, police complaint claim, fear of UAE authorities, and threatening texts in Canada.

propositions.text: RPD found no evidence of targeting or persecution of Sunni Muslims married to Shia Muslims in Pakistan; no evidence such marriages are illegal or persecuted.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found no evidence of persecution or discrimination against Sunni-Shia marriages in Pakistan.

propositions.text: RPD rejected Applicants' refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the applicants' refugee claim.

propositions.text: Issues: 1) Did RPD err by framing claim as interfaith marriage fear? 2) Did RPD err in credibility findings? 3) Did RPD err by not performing separate section 97 analysis?

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies three issues: framing of claim, credibility findings, and section 97 analysis by the RPD.

propositions.text: IRPA sections 96 and 97 define Convention refugee and person in need of protection respectively, with criteria for persecution and risk.

paragraphs.summary: The court states relevant IRPA provisions defining refugee and person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Applicants argue RPD unreasonably limited persecution analysis to interfaith marriage rather than wife's Shia status.
Applicants argue RPD made unreasonable plausibility findings leading to inaccurate negative credibility findings.
Applicants argue RPD misstated and ignored corroborating evidence in credibility findings.
Applicants argue RPD erred by relying on specialized knowledge without opportunity to respond.
Applicants argue RPD erred by not fully analyzing claim under section 97 IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RPD unreasonably limited claim analysis, made flawed credibility findings, relied on specialized knowledge improperly, and failed section 97 analysis.

propositions.text: Respondent argues RPD's negative credibility findings are reasonable due to plausible implausibility findings and lack of corroboration.
Respondent argues RPD did not rely on specialized knowledge improperly and reasonably disbelieved Applicants' allegations.
Respondent argues RPD did not unduly restrict claim analysis; decision must be read as a whole.
Respondent argues RPD did not err by rejecting claim under section 97 without reasons since section 96 has lower standard.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues RPD's credibility findings reasonable, no improper specialized knowledge reliance, no undue restriction, and no error in section 97 rejection.

propositions.text: All three issues reviewed on reasonableness standard as they involve mixed law and fact and factual findings by RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The court states all issues are reviewed on reasonableness standard due to mixed law and fact findings by RPD.

propositions.text: Applicants submit RPD erred by restricting claim to interfaith marriage rather than wife's Shia status.
Court finds RPD considered targeting of Shia Muslims in Pakistan and UNHCR guidelines recognizing protection needs of Shia community.
Court concludes RPD did not unreasonably restrict claim analysis to interfaith marriage only.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue claim restricted to interfaith marriage; court finds RPD considered Shia targeting and did not restrict claim unreasonably.

propositions.text: RPD made negative credibility finding that Principal Applicant's 2012 Pakistan visit narrative was fabricated based on implausibility findings.

RPD found implausible: i) abduction by Islamic group; ii) police refusal to register complaint; iii) fear of deportation preventing UAE authority approach; iv) deliberate car accidents; v) no phone number change after threats; vi) no phone number change upon Canada arrival; vii) no reporting threats to Canadian authorities.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found Principal Applicant's narrative fabricated due to multiple implausibility findings including abduction, police complaint, fear, accidents, phone number, and reporting.

propositions.text: Principal Applicant submits RPD's adverse credibility findings unsupported by evidence; great deference owed to RPD's plausibility findings.
Plausibility findings require clear implausibility and reliable evidentiary base (Pavlov v Canada).
RPD must consider claimant's milieu and culture in plausibility findings (Valtchev v Canada).
Court agrees plausibility findings are necessary and must be based on significant subjective or objective evidence.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RPD's credibility findings unsupported; court cites case law on plausibility and milieu; court agrees plausibility findings necessary and evidence-based.

propositions.text: Except possibly First Information Report issue, RPD's negative plausibility findings are reasonable and supported by evidence considering Applicants' milieu.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD's negative plausibility findings reasonable and supported except possibly for First Information Report issue.

propositions.text: RPD's implausibility finding on lack of First Information Report is questionable as registration often requires bribe; RPD did not inquire further.
Despite this, lack of First Information Report not central; RPD relied on other evidence to reasonably disbelieve Applicants' narrative.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds RPD's First Information Report implausibility questionable but not central; other evidence supports negative credibility finding.

propositions.text: Court's role is to review RPD decision as a whole, not line-by-line for errors (citing Communications, Energy and Paperworkers Union and Kanthasamy).

paragraphs.summary: Court states its role is to review RPD decision as a whole, not line-by-line for errors, citing precedent.

propositions.text: The RPD's state protection analysis applied equally to sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA
No need for RPD to make a separate analysis under section 97 of the IRPA
Court is satisfied RPD considered criteria applicable for each section
Karafazlioglu v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2016 FC 302 at para 13 supports this approach
Bellingy v Canada (Citizenship and Immigration), 2015 FC 1252 at para 53 supports this approach

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's state protection analysis applied equally to IRPA sections 96 and 97, so no separate section 97 analysis was needed, citing Karafazlioglu and Bellingy.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is dismissed
There is no serious question of general importance to be certified

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application for judicial review and finds no serious question of general importance to certify.
